A command typed inside the AI app itself, such as ``/mcp auth``.

Some clients run their OAuth flow only from their own prompt, so the
step has no shell command to copy. Rendering it as a shell command
would be a lie, and burying it in prose is what hid the login step in
the first place, so it is its own kind. The value is public-only: an
in-app prompt is not an approved credential sink, and the repository
additionally pins it to slash-command form so this kind can never be
used to smuggle a shell invocation past the executable registry.

ContextMediaAttachmentPayload.description:
One row of the workspace attachment listing.

Two deliberate departures from ``ContextMediaOrphanPayload``:

``media_type`` is a plain ``str`` and ``kind`` is carried alongside it. The
orphan payload narrows the type to ``ContextImageMediaType`` (four image
literals), but ``context_media_asset.kind`` already admits ``audio`` and
``video``. A workspace-wide listing is exactly where the first non-image
asset would appear, and a ``Literal`` there turns that row into a 500 on
response validation rather than a row the reader can act on.

``can_delete`` answers "may THIS caller delete this now", not just the
domain's usage question -- the page-scoped listing can publish the bare
domain answer because that route is editor-gated, while this one is
readable by a viewer.

ContextMediaOrphanPayload.description:

``created_for_version_id`` names a version whose own status is
``"editing"``) is never listed here at all -- that is an upload in
progress, not an orphan.

Not retention-gated -- every current orphan is listed regardless of
age; only automatic removal (the ``context_media_orphan_sweep`` job) is
gated by ``DTXWIKI_CONTEXT_MEDIA_ORPHAN_RETENTION_HOURS``.

get.description:
Cross-workspace job listing for the operator screen: terminal
failures with a stable ``error_code``, jobs running past their lease, and
everything ``manual retry`` needs. Not workspace-scoped -- that is
``GET /workspaces/{id}/jobs`` -- this is the server-admin surface.

A workspace whose data store cannot be reached is skipped rather than
failing the whole listing; its id is returned in
``unreachable_workspace_ids`` alongside a ``job_fanout_incomplete``
envelope warning, so the caller can tell "short because that is all there
is" apart from "short because part of the fleet did not answer".

Instance-wide background-job queue depth, counted across every
workspace. Server-admin only. There is no per-workspace counterpart:
``GET /workspaces/{id}/jobs`` pages through one workspace's individual
jobs and returns no counts.

A workspace whose data store cannot be reached is left out of the counts
instead of failing the request: its id is returned in
``unreachable_workspace_ids`` and the envelope carries a
``job_fanout_incomplete`` warning. Without that pairing an operator would
read a partial queue depth as a genuinely quiet queue.

post.description:
Requeue a terminally-failed job for one more attempt. Server-admin only.

``retry_count`` is NOT reset -- attempts accumulate, so this retry does
not start a fresh retry cycle: the job's very next failure spends the
last of its budget and fails it terminally again.

Only job types whose failure state lives entirely on the job row can be
requeued; ``retryable`` on each listed job says which, and any other type
is rejected rather than restarted. ``workspace_id`` is required and must
be the workspace that owns ``job_id`` -- the admin listing returns it on
every row. A ``workspace_id`` that does not own the job is answered
exactly like an unknown job, so this endpoint cannot be used to discover
which workspace a job id belongs to.

post.description:
RFC 7009 OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation.

Body (application/x-www-form-urlencoded):
  ``token`` — required, the token to revoke
  ``token_type_hint`` — optional, ``access_token`` | ``refresh_token``
  ``client_id`` — optional, lets a native client revoke its own token

Auth (any one of):
  (1) ``Authorization: Bearer <PAT>`` (``dtxw_`` prefix) → may revoke
      only the authenticated user's own tokens.
  (2) ``Authorization: Bearer <session>`` (cookie or header) → same.
  (3) Form ``client_id`` matches the token's recorded client_id (native
      token-only client owns its own tokens).

Response:
  200 ``{}`` on revoke success OR unknown token (RFC 7009 §2.2).
  401 with WWW-Authenticate header on auth failure (RFC 7009 §2.1).
  400 when the ``token`` field is missing.

Wrong-user bearer auth is treated as ``unknown token`` and returns 200 to
avoid revealing token existence to unauthorised callers. Native
``client_id`` mismatch without bearer auth returns the same 401 challenge as
missing auth because the client self-revoke condition is not satisfied.
